result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.remove_selfloops()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Remove all self-loops from the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1087-L1164){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.remove_selfloops() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A self-loop is an edge where the source and target nodes are the same. This method removes all such edges from the graph, which is a common preprocessing step for many graph algorithms that assume simple graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Remove self-loops from a graph: ::: {#4d9fc1a4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="A") # Self-loop .add_edge(source="B", target="B") # Self-loop ) # Before: 3 edges g.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: After removal: ::: {#5865db90 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="A") .add_edge(source="B", target="B") .remove_selfloops() ) # Only A-B edge remains g.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Use in preprocessing pipeline: ::: {#0a0f3c03 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="X") .add_node(label="Y") .add_node(label="Z") .add_edge(source="X", target="Y") .add_edge(source="Y", target="Z") .add_edge(source="X", target="X") # Self-loop .remove_selfloops() ) # Graph is now simple (assuming no multi-edges) g.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} - works for both directed and undirected graphs. - does not affect multi-edges (use `remove_duplicate_edges()` or `simplify()` for those). - use `which_loops()` to identify self-loops before removal. - use `count_loops()` to count self-loops per node before removal.
